extraction.name: EuroSAT
extraction.description: A novel dataset based on Sentinel-2 satellite images covering 13 spectral bands and consisting of 10 classes with in total 27,000 labeled and geo-referenced images for land use and land cover classification.
extraction.creator: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth
extraction.publisher: TU Kaiserslautern, German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI)
extraction.citeAs: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth. EuroSAT: A Novel Dataset and Deep Learning Benchmark for Land Use and Land Cover Classification. arXiv:1709.00029v2 [cs.CV] 1 Feb 2019
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Satellite images were gathered from European cities distributed in over 34 countries. Images were downloaded from Sentinel-2A satellite via Amazon S3. Satellite images associated with cities covered in the European Urban Atlas were selected. Images with a low cloud level were selected to improve the chance of getting valuable image patches.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Sentinel-2A satellite images provided in the Earth observation program Copernicus. Images were obtained via Amazon S3. The satellite images are openly and freely accessible multi-spectral images covering 13 spectral bands with spatial resolution of up to 10 meters per pixel.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Images recorded all over the year to get high variance. Satellite images from Sentinel-2A satellite launched in June 2015.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Bands with a lower spatial resolution have been upsampled to 10 meters per pixel using cubic-spline interpolation. RGB images were computed by combining the bands red (B04), green (B03) and blue (B02).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Image patches measuring 64x64 pixels were extracted from satellite images. All 27,000 images were manually checked multiple times and corrected by sorting out mislabeled images as well as images full of snow or ice. The dataset has not received atmospheric correction.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Image patches were labeled based on 10 different land use and land cover classes. Classes were selected based on the principle that they showed to be visible at the resolution of 10 meters per pixel and are frequently enough covered by the European Urban Atlas. All 27,000 images were manually checked multiple times and the ground truth was corrected by sorting out mislabeled images.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The classification system opens a gate towards a number of Earth observation applications including agriculture, disaster recovery, climate change, urban development, and environmental monitoring. Applications include land use and land cover change detection and assistance in improving geographical maps.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Within one class of the EuroSAT dataset, different land types of this class are represented. Between the classes, there is a low positive correlation. The classes most common to each other are the two agricultural classes and the two classes representing residential and industrial buildings. The dataset composition is influenced by the number of represented cities per country in the European Urban Atlas.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: A classification system trained with 64x64 image patches does not allow a finely graduated per-pixel segmentation. The dataset has not received atmospheric correction which can result in images with a color cast. The dataset is based on a spatial resolution of 10 meters per pixel which is lower than very-high-resolution datasets.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. The dataset can be used for land use and land cover classification, land use and land cover change detection, and assistance in keeping geographical maps up-to-date. The dataset can be leveraged for multiple real-world Earth observation applications.
